angle: MailerLite kept 'Lite' in its name while adding five products — the homepage tells the story of how it managed that contradiction. The defining tension is: platform expansion vs simplicity brand promise, and the 'Keeping it Lite' section heading is how they resolved it on the page.
distinct_from: creator economy ICP via nav segments
h1: MailerLite Added Five Products and Kept Calling Itself 'Lite' — Here's What the Homepage Shows

sections.goal: Open with the contradiction: 'Lite' brand name, five-product H1. Name the company, period, and the 'Keeping it Lite' section as the key strategic signal. Give the reader a reason to keep reading.

sections.custom_h2: ## MailerLite's homepage arc 2015–2026: from email-only to five-product platform
sections.goal: Show the visual progression from minimal email-focused page to platform homepage. Anchor to the 2015 screenshot (simple), the 2019 mid-point (expansion signs), and 2026 (full platform with 'Keeping it Lite' promise). The payoff is the contrast.

sections.custom_h2: ## How MailerLite's H1 went from one product to five — and what they added to manage it
sections.goal: Analyze the H1 expansion (email → five products) and the 'Keeping it Lite' + support headings as complexity-management signals. Explain what the five-category H1 assumes about the visitor's awareness level vs what a single-product H1 assumes.

sections.custom_h2: ## How MailerLite's CTAs and navigation shifted the sales motion
sections.goal: Analyze the dual-CTA setup (Sign up free + Watch demo) as a hybrid PLG/sales motion. Explain the audience-segment navigation ('Solopreneurs', 'Small business') as ICP naming — unusual in SaaS nav. End with a founder test about nav item naming.

sections.custom_h2: ## Why MailerLite kept 'Lite' while building a five-product platform
sections.goal: Explain the Mailchimp complexity problem MailerLite was responding to. Cover the creator economy bifurcation (Kit, Beehiiv, Ghost). Explain why keeping 'Lite' in the brand was the right call given who they were competing with.

sections.custom_h2: ## What SaaS teams can study from MailerLite's homepage evolution
sections.goal: 3 patterns: (1) audience-segment nav items, (2) naming the complexity objection as a homepage section, (3) dual CTA for hybrid PLG/sales motion. Each pattern must be anchored to MailerLite's specific evidence and end with a runnable test.
